verses.verse:
यदा बशं सुपक्वं स्यात् तस्य बंशी विशिष्यते।
अणु रन्ध्रेषु नादानाम् स्वयंभूनां च सम्भवात्।।१३।।
verses.text: When the bamboo is well seasoned, the bānsurī made from it excels, because self-born sounds arise in its micro-pores.

commentary.text: As far as the question of a suitable material for the bānsurī goes, bamboo is the best. But even among bamboos, the better one is the bamboo that has matured (supakva, well seasoned) thoroughly and naturally. For in ripe bamboo, compared with green bamboo, the aṇurandhra (micro-pores), that is the fine fibres, become more distinct, and its capacity for supporting sound is also greater. Now the question is of making the bānsurī.

Today, among bānsurī players, those artists who do not know how to make a bānsurī are unhappy. The problem before them is whom to have a bānsurī made by, one that is true in tune and matches the desired pitch. If I have to play together in some ensemble, all the instruments will have one fixed pitch, and if my bānsurī does not match it, then I shall have to seek the help of a skilled nirmātā (maker) who can make a bānsurī as I want it. This problem can be fully solved only when artists make their own bānsurīs. So now I shall set out the proper rules for making a bānsurī, which by the grace of [my] guru I found after searching for years.

subsection.title: The Kinds of Bānsurī and Suitable Materials
